# Tools referenced by this skill

- [BitBucket](https://bitbucket.org/) - Bitbucket is used for hosting and managing source code repositories, primarily using Git, and is designed to help software development teams collaborate on code, automate builds and deployments with Bitbucket Pipelines, and integrate with other tools like Jira.
- [Calendar Versioning](https://calver.org/) - Calendar Versioning (CalVer) is a versioning convention based on your project's release calendar, instead of arbitrary numbers.
- [Docker](https://www.docker.com/) - Docker is a tool for creating isolated environments (application isolation) for software development called containers to enable consistent software running across platforms. Docker allows developers to build, share, run and verify applications easily. DockerHub is a repository for sharing and managing container images.
- [Dockstore](https://dockstore.org/) - Dockstore is a free and open source platform for sharing reusable and scalable analytical bioinformatics tools and workflows.
- [GitHub](https://github.com/) - GitHub is a platform that allows developers to create, store, manage, and share their code. It uses Git to provide distributed version control. GitHub provides access control, bug tracking, software feature requests, task management, continuous integration, and wikis for every project.
- [GitLab](https://about.gitlab.com/) - DevOps platform that enables teams to collaborate, plan, develop, test, and deploy software using an integrated toolset for version control, CI/CD, and project management.
- [Guix](https://guix.gnu.org/) - Package manager.
- [NixOS](https://nixos.org/) - NixOS is a free and open-source Linux distribution based on the Nix package manager. It uses declarative configuration (using the Nix language) to manage packages and the entire system environment - allowing for reproducibility and portability.
- [ReproZip](https://www.reprozip.org/) - ReproZip automatically packs research along with all necessary data files, libraries, environment variables and options into a self-contained bundle which can be used to set up the same original environment so anybody can reproduce the research on a different machine, without tracking down and installing the dependencies, or even having to run the same operating system.
- [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) - Semantic versioning (SemVer) is a widely-adopted version scheme that encodes a version of a project by a three-part version number (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH), an optional pre-release tag, and an optional build meta tag.
- [SingularityCE](https://sylabs.io/singularity/) - Singularity is an open source container platform allows us to create and run containers that package up pieces of software in a way that is portable and reproducible. Singularity is designed for ease-of-use on shared multiuser systems and in High Performance Computing (HPC) environments. Singularity is compatible with all Docker images and it can be used with GPUs and MPI applications.
- [Software Heritage](https://www.softwareheritage.org) - Software Heritage archive is the largest public collection of source code in existence. It Collects, preserves, curates and makes available software in source code form as cultural heritage
- [WorkflowHub](https://workflowhub.eu/) - WorkflowHub is a registry for describing, sharing and publishing scientific computational workflows.
- [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/) - Zenodo is a general-purpose open repository developed under the European OpenAIRE program and operated by CERN. It allows researchers to deposit research papers, data sets, research software, reports, and other research-related digital artefacts.
